steps.content: The breeze sweeps over the wreckage, torn apart and stitched back together, and your gaze crosses the broken ground to settle on her.
Is it because you've only just come back? Your vision blurs. You cannot see her face, only the hem of her robe stirring gently in the wind.
Behind you, a voice tinged with warmth reaches your ears.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Go on.
You walk toward her, dragging your steps on purpose.
When she found you that first time, weren't you lying just like this in the mud, perfectly still? What had she done then? Shaken a bell and chanted some nonsense incantation, hadn't she?
You crouch down. The bell rests between you, its clapper choked with mud, silent. You gently brush it aside.
No response.
You clasp her cold wrist and pull her arm across your shoulder, hoisting her onto your back. She weighs less than you imagined, even for a child's frame.
You lift your head. The man before you is still watching with that same soft smile. Did he see this ending coming too? And even knowing it, can he still face it with something like peace?
The answer doesn't matter anymore. Slowly, you walk toward him.
[Transition 2s]
...Heh.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Am I heavy?
Your heart trembles. You bite down on your lip and force your spine straighter.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Not at all.
The words have barely left you when the weight on your shoulders vanishes. A rustle of fabric sounds beside you, soft and stirring, so achingly familiar that your tears almost drop.

She bends down, bringing her eyes level with yours, and studies you with earnest care. Then she reaches out and wipes your cheek, but the blood on her fingertips only smears across your skin. She offers you a sheepish smile.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Well. After all that, I still needed you to carry me back. That's just embarrassing.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: One might hope a certain someone would take a lesson from this.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: A lesson? Honestly, it could've gone a lot worse. You know me. I bounce back.
She stands, wobbling for a moment before steadying herself.
Her hand lifts, fingers reaching for the spot just below her ear, but there is nothing left to find. Only tiny specks of dust float between her fingers in the light.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Well? The sacred relic of the Tianyi Sect's did the trick, didn't it? A good thing I insisted you bring it along.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: What's with that tone? I didn't know you were so proud of the old sect.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Have to say though, I didn't expect it to be that useful. Hmm... think I could order them in bulk?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: And do what, exactly? Stock up enough to storm the Void of Yin a hundred more times and fling the gates of the underworld wide open?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Don't tempt me. I might just try it.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Utterly hopeless.
Chengxiao shakes his head, his voice tinged with resignation.
Yet something in the unseen world compels you to turn around. Even as you walk step by step toward the light, those whispers have already rooted themselves deep within your mind.
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Turn back... look back...
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Everything you treasure... everything you love... it's all here...
Two dark silhouettes flicker behind you.
No human could resist such a call. But...
[Tremor]
Lichen staggers, and you immediately brace her with your shoulder. She hesitates for just a moment, then wraps her arms around you in turn.
[CG]

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Well, look at that. Turns out I still need you to keep me upright after all.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: You seem to be recovering remarkably fast. Right back to your old self, I see.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: What can I say? This one's my auspicious star.
She grins brazenly, still leaning into you, though the burden on your shoulder has lightened just a bit.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Go back and recover your strength first. After that, you owe the expedition team an apology. And you'll need to send a message back to the sect explaining the situation. You've stirred up quite a commotion across the Eastern Continent. They will have certainly sensed something amiss by now.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Just a message? What about telling them what we actually found? A chance to clear our names for once.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Clear our names? You mean tell them that after the Man-Fiend incident, two disciples of the Tianyi Sect, Lichen and Chengxiao, very nearly succumbed to corruption, and only narrowly escaped with their lives thanks to the aid of some mysterious stranger from the West...

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Surely you don't actually believe you've succeeded.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You really know how to kill a good mood, you know that?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hey, speaking of which, where's the little curly-haired one?
A familiar figure bounds up in the distance, rushing a few steps your way before skidding to an abrupt halt. That messy head of curls whirls around in a circle, directionless.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: What's he doing all the way over there?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: I told him to go on ahead. It seems he's been waiting for us all the same. Though I suspect he's keeping his distance for fear we might be phantoms.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: This works out rather well. We can each go with a partner.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: And don't think you can change the subject. You will sit down and write that letter to the sect, properly. I will not have you sending the elders into apoplexy again.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: We'll see.
The words stop short. A hand comes to rest lightly on the crown of your head.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: We've been going on about things you couldn't follow again, haven't we?
You blink, realizing you had drifted off entirely. You didn't hear a word.
You were too absorbed in the weight resting against your shoulder, the gentle heat of aging sunlight, and the sound of their voices, still warm and bright, before time could wear them thin.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Let us head back. When you return, get some proper rest, won't you?
Lichen clears her throat, presses her fingers together, and speaks in a slow, lilting cadence:

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The hour is most auspicious. Allow me to cast one last divination for you. Let me see... our little auspicious star...

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Tonight, your dreams will be nothing but sweet.
So let the story pause here for now.
Now, grip the hand in yours and move forward. Don't look back. The whispers and phantoms behind you have lost their power to harm.
If all of this was really fated, then we will meet again at the end.
[Black Screen 2s]
[Chief's Lounge]

Following the conclusion of the latest Illusory Moon tide, ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC, regained consciousness after the nightmare's grip released. The Bureau immediately conducted a full medical evaluation. The findings confirmed that the Chief's physical and mental faculties showed no irregularities.

The precise cause of the anomalous fluctuations observed during this Illusory Moon cycle remains unresolved. Nevertheless, the Chief managed to retrieve a considerable amount of highly valuable research data during the mission. These documents have now been transferred to the research department, and a thorough analysis has commenced.
[DisCity Central Library]
After the incident concluded, the Chief filed a formal request to review historical records pertaining to the expedition, archived at the DisCity Central Library.
[Verifying clearance level] Access granted
[CG]

<color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>, birth name Li Xianling, was formerly a Daoist priestess of the Eastern Continent. In the years after the Perishing Star fell, she journeyed across the Eastern Continent, gathering folklore and documenting anomalous phenomena associated with it. Her work focused on investigating the potential connection between human spiritual activity and the Perishing Star.

In ▉▉, she volunteered for the expedition and subsequently served as an advisor representing the Eastern Continent, offering specialized support to related operations.

She went missing in ▉▉ during Operation ▉▉. When exhaustive search efforts failed to locate her, she was officially declared <color=#fb9259>deceased</color>.
[CG]

<color=#fb9259>Chengxiao</color>, birth name Lyu Buzhou, was a researcher of mysticism at the Eastern Continent University. His academic career centered on religion, belief systems, and the human psyche. After the Perishing Star fell, he turned his focus to the spiritual and psychological anomalies emerging across various regions in the disaster's aftermath.

He joined the expedition in ▉▉, thereafter contributing his expertise as a mysticism researcher of the Eastern Continent.

He went missing in ▉▉ during Operation ▉▉. When exhaustive search efforts failed to locate him, he was officially declared <color=#fb9259>deceased</color>.
[Daoist Temple]

[Records on the Tianyi Sect, compiled by Eastian scholars]

Eastian scholars report that the <color=#fb9259>Tianyi Sect</color> ceased to exist many years ago. Its esoteric arts are nonetheless widely acknowledged as the foundation of <color=#fb9259>the seer legend</color>, though later seized and restricted by the seers who followed. The <color=#fb9259>seer</color> practices now current in Eastia are largely imitations and adaptations derived from the Tianyi Sect's original methods.

The original creator of these arts vanished long ago, with some accounts claiming they fled Eastia in fear of the disaster and were never seen again.

After several calamities, related records were further scattered across Eastia, making complete recovery nearly impossible.

Following investigation and review, only a handful of annotated fragments have been recovered. Though these surviving pages contain references tied to <color=#fb9259>the seer legend</color>, the lack of definitive dates, authorship, and complete context precludes any verification of their authenticity at present. Consequently, they do not qualify for formal archival inclusion.

Nevertheless, considering that these fragments were discovered by chance among a batch of old books slated for mass incineration, and that they still possess a degree of preservation value, transferring them to DisCity for safekeeping within the Bureau's database may be the more prudent approach.

[On the Calamities of Primordial Chaos, Volume IV]

...Practical observation confirms that so-called calamities are Wraith Beasts coalesced from human consciousness, and that they disintegrate when that same consciousness crumbles. If this principle can be harnessed to exert reverse control over the force of <color=#fb9259>collective will</color> to its maximum extent, it may be possible for human beings, in their mortal bodies, to oppose calamity itself.

...To accomplish this, three elements are essential: the people, the ritual, and the vessel.

Neatly written annotation: The sect has already run small-scale trials, though the method appears quite limited at this stage. Firstly, crafting the vessels requires specific materials. While those they used bear a broadly similar structural makeup to the artifacts we uncovered in the Void of Yin, their efficacy is far inferior. What accounts for this disparity requires further study. Another challenge is finding someone capable of presiding over the rituals and subduing the Wraith Beasts. As I noted before, formally conferring a title upon such individuals is equally essential. I sent you several name proposals earlier. You read them and never replied. Hastily scrawled annotation: All that beating around the bush just to say we need to go back into Maria City for another look? I'll join the next expedition. As for the names... the ones you came up with are all so uninspired. "Priest" sounds like something out of the West, and "Ritual Officer" lacks any sense of mystery. ...What if we called them seers?
[Sun Crow CG]

In N.F. 106, a devastating drought fell upon Eastia. The following year, the Apostle of Ashes known as <color=#fb9259>Sun Crow</color> manifested. The seer <color=#fb9259>Xu</color> gave herself to the Apostle, merging with it entirely and succeeding in containing its rampage.
[Sun Crow Background]

In N.F. 112, the Tide of Ashes struck Eastia, destroying several city-states and submerging large areas of land. The next year, the Apostle of Ashes <color=#fb9259>Sun Crow</color> broke its seal, and by N.F. 114 it reached DisCity, trying to enter the DisSea. At the same time, Eastia sent a delegation to DisCity seeking cooperation.

In the end, with help from Eastian Sinners <color=#fb9259>Yao</color>, <color=#fb9259>Du Ruo</color>, <color=#fb9259>Yanyan</color>, and all of FAC, ${PlayerName}, Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, successfully eliminated the Sun Crow Apostle.

The operation also gathered more critical data on the Apostles of Ashes for DisCity and established friendly relations with Eastia. The data will be used in future operations against the Apostles of Ashes.
[Bureau]
In N.F. ▉▉▉, two S-Class Sinners advanced upon the DisSea perimeter. The Bureau acted immediately, establishing preliminary containment of both targets and securing their successful detention.
The profiles of the two Sinners are as follows:
[CG]

Sinner <color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>, ID S-396. Corruption level: high. Psychological condition: relatively stable. It should be noted, however, that the subject's soul and physical body are not synchronized on the same frequency. If not for the subject's ongoing self-suppression achieved by burning her own soul, her physical body would constitute a major threat.
[CG]

Sinner <color=#fb9259>Chengxiao</color>, ID S-159. Corruption level: high. Psychological condition: relatively stable. It should be noted, however, that the subject's soul and physical body are not synchronized on the same frequency. If not for the subject's continuous self-binding through ritual sorcery, his physical body would constitute a major threat.
[Chief's Office]

Since their admission into custody, neither Sinner has caused any harm, whether within the Bureau or beyond it. Their anomalous conditions have remained largely within controllable parameters.

Given that both Sinners are classified at the extreme threat level, the Bureau will maintain ongoing observation and documentation of their respective states.

[MBCC Daily Report]

No unusual activity reported today.
All is well.
[Black Screen]

<size=62><b>The End
City Beyond Tribulation</color>
[Transition 3s]
[Chief's Lounge]
You slide the two thin files into an archival envelope, seal it shut, and ready it for return to the Central Library today, where it will be locked away once more.
The little black triangle peeks cautiously around the doorframe, observing you for a while before drifting slowly to your desk and giving a fawning little wag.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The Illusory Moon's cycle shifted without any warning this time. You had to face two S-Class Sinners all on your own, and you didn't just walk away in one piece. You brought back a goldmine of intel. I shouldn't be surprised, Chief. But I still am.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No, not just two. There was someone else. We had to pair up to get out, so there should've been four of us. He was...
[Keylan's character art fades to black]
But his features and the sound of his voice are already starting to blur.
...Don't worry if it⬛⬛⬛... ⬛ big team... ⬛remember⬛important⬛.. Don't ⬛⬛...doesn't ring a bell.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: He was...?
It darts up to your face in an instant, activates recording mode, and begins bobbing eagerly, brimming with anticipation.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Sorry. I can't remember.
The little black triangle droops with a soft beep, but it seems to console itself quickly enough, twirling around on the spot.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: You've clearly overclocked yourself. Go get some proper rest. The full report can wait until you're awake.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: A brain like yours doesn't just lose things. I'm sure the important bits are all in there.
But in the end, you let it down.
Try as you might, the face and name of the third person you met in that dream never come back to you.
